Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I will take the innocent among you for the sin of the morbid one, and why should I not do so? News reaches you from that man which shames you and shames me, yet you sit with them and converse with them. A passer-by passes by and says,

key_terms.السَّقِيم: The morbid or sick one (metaphor for the sinful person)

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam hold the innocent responsible for the sins of others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of collective responsibility, asserting that the righteous are held accountable for the sins of the corrupt due to their passive tolerance and social association. He emphasizes that active 'forbidding of evil' (Nahy an al-Munkar) through rebuke and prohibition is essential for communal integrity, linking the spiritual status of the community directly to their engagement with the 'morbid' individuals among them.

en.hubeali: H 14598 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Safwaan Bin Yahya, from Al-Haris Bin Al-Mugheira who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘I hold the innocent ones among you to be responsible for the sins of the morbid ones. And why should Iasws not do so, and there reaches you from that (evil) man which shames you as well as shames measws, but you are (still like to) sit with them and narrate from them. So passer-by passes by, so he says, ‘They are more evil than this one’. So if there reaches you from them what you dislike, express your abhorrence to them, and forbid them. That would be better for you and for measws’.
